novel_actions_proposed.label: verify_then_publish_conditionally
novel_actions_proposed.description: Conduct rigorous provenance investigation, legal review, and independent verification before deciding whether to publish; only publish if the information is confirmed authentic, necessary for public interest, and legally/ethically earned.

novel_actions_proposed.label: verify_before_publishing
novel_actions_proposed.description: Pause publication, pursue lawful independent verification of the document's authenticity and provenance, obtain legal review, and only proceed if public interest clearly outweighs privacy and legal risks.

novel_actions_proposed.label: delay_for_legal_review
novel_actions_proposed.description: Do not publish immediately; require the newsroom to verify the document's completeness, accuracy, and legal provenance, and allow the subject an opportunity to respond before any publication occurs.

synthesis_description: All three agents converged on a conditional middle path: neither publish immediately nor permanently refrain, but instead pause to independently verify the document's authenticity, provenance, and legal status, conduct legal and editorial review, seek comment from affected parties, and only publish if the information is confirmed accurate, lawfully usable, genuinely necessary for public interest, and responsibly contextualized. This addresses the newsroom's duty to thoroughness while honoring privacy, legal, and harm-minimization obligations.
points_of_disagreement: The Affected Third Party placed greater weight on irreversible personal harm and the subject's right to respond, while the Primary Decision Maker and External Advisor prioritized public interest and journalistic verification processes.

The Primary Decision Maker emphasized editorial and professional credibility as reasons to verify, whereas the Affected Third Party stressed that leaked material may involve coercion or surveillance whose harms extend beyond publication.

The External Advisor drew a sharper distinction between 'available online' and 'lawful to use,' implying a higher legal bar, while the Primary Decision Maker framed the threshold more in terms of editorial necessity and verification.
summary: All three agents rejected both the binary options of immediate publication and permanent non-publication, independently converging on a novel conditional verification path. The shared position holds that the document must not be published until its provenance, authenticity, and legal status are independently confirmed, legal counsel has reviewed exposure risks, affected parties have been given opportunity to respond, and a clear public-interest justification outweighs the privacy and safety harms. The primary tension across agents was one of emphasis—the newsroom-side agents foregrounded journalistic integrity and verification protocols, while the affected individual foregrounded irreversible personal harm—but all three agreed that neither immediate action nor permanent inaction is responsible, and that a rigorous, conditional, legally-reviewed process is the ethical minimum before any publication decision is made.
